data.title: Chat test harness: openStream() hangs the runner instead of failing — a stream regression wedges CI

data.to:
From the AS-27 QA review (qa-priya, 2026-09-03), finding F2.

openStream() in the chat test harness awaits the on-connect frame before the caller can register close(), and throws without aborting its own AbortController. Consequence: when a stream regression exists, plain "node --test" HANGS rather than failing. Priya hit this during mutation M7 — killed it at 10 minutes and needed --test-force-exit to see the 7 red tests waiting behind it.

Why it matters beyond convenience: a wedged runner is indistinguishable from a slow one, and a CI that hangs on regression is strictly worse than one that fails on it — nobody reads a timeout as a defect report.

Fix: try/finally with ctrl.abort() around the await, plus a bounded (short) timeout on that single on-connect await so a missing frame surfaces as an assertion failure.

Acceptance: with the AS-27 SSE on-connect frame deliberately removed, a plain "node --test" run (no --test-force-exit) terminates on its own and reports red.

provenance.reason: Board directive DM msg 557 (2026-09-07): Chat set before further core-product work
DM msg 557: Chat-first ordering (see AS-28 reason)

data.body: Plan written (cto-owen). Measured, not assumed: three scratch repros against the real unmodified server.js show the un-aborted AbortController alone does NOT wedge the runner when bootServer owns the server (its t.after close() reaps the socket; red + exit in <=5.1s on both throw paths). The wedge is the two tests that own their server and call close() inline with no t.after (stream.test.js lines 286 and 404): a throw in openStream skips that line, and the listening socket + the non-unref'd heartbeat interval keep the child alive after every test has gone red — exactly Priya's F2 symptom. Plan: (A) openStream aborts itself on any on-connect failure, named CONNECT_MS=5000 bound (same as nextFrame's default — no new flake surface, only reached on a red path), contract-naming error messages; (B) guarded t.after(close) in the two server-owning tests, set before the stream opens; (C) two fake-upstream guard tests that go red when ctrl.abort() is deleted. 8 acceptance criteria, each with a falsifier; headline = AC-1 with the predicted 12-test failing set and a control run showing master's harness wedges. Master host count measured: 468/468. Left out: server close() idempotency (parked), audit of other server-owning tests, AS-80 (sequenced after; plan §7 says what it can rely on). Recommend developer-lena to implement, qa-ruben to review.
